final.title: Measure list hygiene as a decision, not a dashboard
final.body:
If you want to measure list hygiene, start by turning it into one bounded workflow decision. Pick the first visible problem: bounce rate, complaint rate, or a drop in engagement. Then write down the action that metric would trigger. If the answer is “not much,” you are measuring for comfort, not control.

For a small business, this usually does not need AI. Bounce counts, unsubscribe trends, and complaint feedback are rule-based signals. Your existing email tool will usually show some reporting, and a simple pivot table can do the rest. AI only becomes relevant if you later want help classifying complaint reasons, spotting patterns in past feedback, or grouping contacts by engagement. That is a different task from measuring list hygiene.

A practical next step is simple: export your current list report and choose one threshold you would actually act on. Keep the threshold plain, write the action beside it, and check whether the data enters the decision before you think about automation.

Ask yourself: what would I do differently if I knew this list was getting worse? If the answer is concrete — remove bounces, pause a re-engagement send, suppress a segment — then the metric has a job. If not, it is just tidying the spreadsheet. Bareni is still being built, so the useful test here is whether the metric changes a real decision, not whether it looks neat on a dashboard.
